instruction:
Edit exactly one file: apps/docs/core/functional/plan-and-execute-tasks.mdx. Extend ONLY the body of the section headed `## 5. Use filters to focus`. Change nothing else in the file — not the frontmatter, not any heading, not sections 1-4, not section 6, not the `## Next` list. Do not create any new file. Do not touch apps/docs/docs.json, README.md, or anything under apps/web/src.

CURRENT CONTENT OF SECTION 5 (lines 45-55) — preserve every line of this verbatim, in this order, and add your new prose around/after it:

```
## 5. Use filters to focus

The board toolbar supports filtering by:

- Status
- Priority
- Assignee
- Due date
- Labels

Use filters aggressively during standups, planning, and triage.
```

WHAT TO ADD: user-facing prose describing the active-filter chips that the board toolbar renders. Roughly 10-25 lines of new content. Plain markdown only (paragraphs, bullet list, bold, optionally one simple markdown table) — no MDX imports, no components, no JSX, no images, no screenshots.

The facts you must convey, all verified against the shipped board toolbar:

1. WHEN A CHIP EXISTS. A chip is rendered for a field only while that field has at least one value selected. Each of the five fields gets at most one chip — never one chip per selected value.

2. WHERE CHIPS APPEAR. Chips appear in the board toolbar itself, in the same left-hand row as the **Filter** button and the sort control, after them. That row wraps when it runs out of width. Do NOT say the chips appear on a separate row, in a separate bar, in a filter bar, or below the toolbar. Present them in their render order: Status, Priority, Assignee, Due date, Labels.

3. CHIP ANATOMY. A chip shows four divider-separated segments: the subject (the field name), the operator, the value, and an `X` (clear) control. Refer to the clear control as the chip's `X` control — never identify it by colour or position alone.

4. SUBJECT WORDING. Use the shipped subject strings exactly as written: **Status**, **Priority**, **Assignee**, **Due date**, **Labels**. Note the lowercase "d" in "Due date", matching the existing bullet list.

5. OPERATOR AND VALUE, PER FIELD. These five fields do NOT behave alike; state the differences explicitly. This table is the authority — reproduce its content faithfully in whatever form you choose (a markdown table is acceptable and probably clearest):

| Field | Operator text | Icon preview in the value segment | Value text when exactly ONE value is selected | Value text when TWO OR MORE are selected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Status | is any of | Yes — stacked status/column icons | The column's name | a count, e.g. "3 selected" |
| Priority | is any of | Yes — stacked priority icons | The priority's name | a count, e.g. "3 selected" |
| Assignee | is any of | Yes — stacked member avatars | The member's name | a count, e.g. "3 selected" |
| Due date | is any of | NO icons | The chosen option's name: **Due this week**, **Due next week**, or **No due date** | a count, e.g. "3 selected" |
| Labels | include any of | NO icons | ALWAYS a count, even for a single label — the label is never named | a count, e.g. "3 selected" |

The operator difference must be stated explicitly: Status, Priority, Assignee and Due date chips read **is any of**; the Labels chip reads **include any of**. Do not describe a single uniform operator.

You must explicitly call out two exceptions: (a) the Labels chip never names the selected label — it always shows the count, unlike the other four fields, which name a single selected value; (b) the Due date chip shows no icon preview, unlike Status, Priority and Assignee.

If you mention the icon/avatar preview at all, you must state that at most three icons are shown regardless of how many values are selected, and you must not imply one icon per selected value. Do not attribute an icon preview to the Due date or Labels chip.

The multi-selection text renders as a number followed by the word `selected` — write it as e.g. "3 selected".

6. WHAT THE `X` CLEARS — the rule most easily got wrong. For ALL FIVE fields, including Labels, the chip's `X` clears that field's ENTIRE selection, not a single value: the chip disappears and every value selected for that field is removed. State that the `X` never affects the other four fields' chips — the other chips and their selections are left untouched. Do not suggest the `X` removes one value at a time or that you must click it repeatedly.

7. CLEAR ALL FILTERS. **Clear all filters** is NOT a standalone toolbar button and is NOT part of any chip. It is the last item inside the **Filter** dropdown menu, below a separator, and it is shown only once at least one filter is active. It clears every filter at once. Use the neutral phrasing "once at least one filter is active" rather than enumerating the five fields.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Scope every claim to the board toolbar. Do NOT claim the chips appear in List view, in Backlog, or on the task page. The section's existing opening ("The board toolbar supports filtering by:") sets this scope; stay inside it.
- Terminology: "chip" and "filter chip" ARE permitted as the descriptive noun. Do not invent any other product terminology — no "filter pill", "filter bar", "facet", "token", "filter tray" — and no invented option names.
- Quoted UI strings must match the shipped English strings character for character: "Clear all filters", "is any of", "include any of", "Due this week", "Due next week", "No due date", and a count rendered as "3 selected".
- Do not mention WIP limits, work in progress limits, or hours rollup anywhere.
- Do not document the filter dropdown's internals beyond the location of **Clear all filters** (skip the per-field submenus, the "All statuses"/"All priorities" reset rows, and select-all label behaviour). Do not document sorting, the Board/List view-mode toggle, or backlog filtering.
- Do not claim anything about filter persistence, URL state, or how filtering is applied to the task list.
- Omit internal edge-case fallbacks (unmatched status ids, unresolved assignees).
- House style: short prose, second person, imperative where instructional, matching sections 1-4. Match the surrounding page's markdown conventions.
- Diff hygiene: no reformatting of untouched lines, no trailing-whitespace churn, no reordering of the existing bullets.
